entityDescription:
SERTIT (SErvice Régional de Traitement d'Image et de Télédétection) is a self-funding remote sensing service within the University of Strasbourg, whose legal representative is the President of the University of Strasbourg (UNISTRA) and has recently integrated a large university laboratory ICube as a platform. 
SERTIT is part of ICube Laboratory and Michel de Mathelin is director of both. Hence, SERTIT is now being administered through ICube within the University of Strasbourg. Then, each applications or service domain has an appointed reference leader. SERTIT also has increasing links to other laboratories and departments within the University of Strasbourg.
SERTIT was founded in 1986 with the arrival of the CNES SPOT programme. It is specializes in producing geo-information from Earth Observation data developing image processing methods and delivering geo-information products in natural resources monitoring, land management, urban planning, environmental survey, plus natural disaster and risk management.
SERTIT has a multi-disciplinary team, comprised of 20 specialists in remote sensing, GIS, geology, land surveying, photogrammetry, geography and physics, and proposes professional training for users of Earth Observation Services. SERTIT is both a R&D centre and a service provider. SERTIT has accompanied the development of the whole French EO satellite family (SPOT AVAL projects, Pléiades HR system programmes, ARCTOS system, new CO3D), European Space Agency satellite development (ERS-1, through ENVISAT to the Sentinels) and is Principal Investigator for many space agencies.
SERTIT a rapid mapping pioneer has supported activities within the International Charter “Space and Major Disasters” since 2000. SERTIT is a key player offering rapid mapping to the civil protection, humanitarian communities, insurance actors. Also, in Copernicus EMS Risk and Recovery SERTIT teams with Airbus DS, to provide services.
Otherwise, SERTIT’s work consists of land cover/land use monitoring exploiting EO. Part of this work was focussed on urban growth monitoring and now another part consist in natural resource (grassland and forest) mapping and monitoring in Western Europe: Interreg ForestClim project, forest clearing and logging, storm damage and species mapping.
Since 2002, SERTIT is largely involved in developing EO applications as well as EO training in Asia, particularly in China and Vietnam. SERTIT was PI for the DRAGON I to 3 successful Flood project (2004-2008) and is now working on DRAGON 4. The common word is “water driven landscape” and cover the field of vegetation mapping, biodiversity assessment, water quality, water extent, water resource monitoring and epidemiology.
At last, SERTIT is involved in training activities, participates in Master courses and training. It is also involved in training sessions for European Space agency in Europe (Lisbon Prague Krakow) and China (Wuhan, Lanzhou), training actions funded by the French Foreign office (Catachina in Beijing, 2003, Bulgarisk in 2009), CNES training programmes in Mexico (2014) and Haiti (2015) and for Algerian agencies (2016).
SERTIT is also working on 3D applications involving satellite and drone imagery and is leading the A²S project (Alsace Aval Sentinelle), which focuses on the development and the implementation of a value added production centre exploiting large Sentinel data fluxes.
SERTIT always takes user wishes and needs into account converging user requirements and expectations with EO data potential and processing methods to conceive adapted products and services. As an independent entity, it uses space for Earth’s benefit helping spread Europe’s influence. SERTIT enables the following worlds to converge : space domain technologies and their users; remote sensing research and industrial applications; researchers from all over the world; and political and economic players.

entityDescription: The Parco Archeologico di Ostia Antica is one of the new institution with administrative autonomy of the Italian Ministry of Culture. It is one of the largest archaeological parks of the Country, including the remains of the most important seaport of ancient Rome, the largest harbour of the ancient Mediterranean, practically the “hub” of the Roman empire from the early centuries of the city life, until the late antiquity, on which the Park mainly exercises tasks of protection, promotion and enhancement. The most important archaeological sites of the Park are: the ruins of ancient city of Ostia; the necropolis of Isola Sacra; the complex of the Imperial ports of Claudius and Trajan (Portus), the two basilicas of Portus and S. Ippolito and the Late Antiquity and Medieval Age remains of the city of Portus, the Museum of Roman Ships near the international airport “Leonardo da Vinci” of Fiumicino. The Parco is one of the main research centers on the ancient logistics.
